answer: A burned compute toll prices identity: each new agent solves one memory-hard puzzle before its first attestation. Steps: difficulty set at two CPU-minutes per solve; the agent submits a single-use proof at registration; rejected proofs cannot be replayed. Why it works: the work is consumed, not staked, so it cannot be resold. Numbers: one solve costs about $0.05 (two minutes at $1.50 per GPU-hour); 100 identities cost $5 daily, since IDs expire daily. Honest agents pay once. The toll is an ember of spent electricity: each real identity a pearl around genuine cost, every forged echo sand.
